summary: Port Coulomb impulse scaling, ordered cached body warmstart gathering and split-slot warmstart application with native graph buffers.
regressions: All three Rust entry points at 0/1/31/32/33/63/64/65/129 constraints with three dispatches
Distinct cache and recomputed deltas, both sides, reversed adjacency, permuted constraint IDs, empty points, shared static/dynamic bodies, hub skip and split-slot indirection
Runtime multi-batch body lengths, final bucket constraint count, coefficients zero/one/fractional, capacity-clipped hub slots and untouched sentinel storage
Exact cache tags, padding and write_constraint resets; malformed graphs, layouts, tags, uniforms and output writes rejected
Cancellation-sensitive cached accumulation rejects reordered adjacency summation; mutable local buffers avoid invalid guarded Metal scalar assignment and repeated CPU interval-analysis expansion.
differences: No changes to Rust physics or existing tolerances. Three isolated entry points do not complete production solver/frame scheduling.
The shared tiled warmstart helper reuses the identical force/torque arithmetic from TwoBodyConstraint while preserving the extra zero-based delta then velocity-add order of the Rust hub entry point.
Read/write constraint roundtrip is specialized to the actually changed impulse fields, inactive coupling zeros, model-specific header zeros and cache. All preserved storage is guarded bitwise.
Native uniforms are represented as readonly u32 storage buffers in replay; all offsets derive from the live Rust exporter. Empty fixtures specialize a no-op before compiler index analysis.
Gather start and hub mapped index use one-element local buffers to work around compiler issues; no arithmetic order or native layout changes.
